title: Ginger (Green): modeled ₹658/qtl left, Kattappana → Kottakkal
summary: February 2021: reported ginger (Green) prices at Kattappana and Kottakkal imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 94% of 16 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹658 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 288 same-variety market pairs screened for ginger (Green) in February 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kottakkal report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: February 2021
scenes.caption: Kattappana (Kerala) and Kottakkal (Kerala) both reported ginger (Green) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 16 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kattappana reported a median ₹2,500 per quintal. Kottakkal reported a median ₹3,650 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,050/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,050 per quintal, and Kottakkal was dearer on 94% of days.

scenes.headline: 254 km by road
scenes.caption: 254 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹55/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹677 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹484 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kottakkal report, the rule selects 15 of 16 modeled shipping days. 15 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹658 per quintal (₹462 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Ginger (Green) route from Kattappana to Kottakkal was positive on 94% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹65,800, or ₹46,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to ginger (Green)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹55/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Ginger (Green) route from Kattappana to Kottakkal was positive on 94% of matched days in February 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹65,800, or ₹46,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Ginger (Green): modeled ₹727/qtl left, Solan → Hamirpur (Nadaun)
summary: December 2021: reported ginger (Green) prices at Solan and Hamirpur (Nadaun) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 93% of 14 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹727 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 300 same-variety market pairs screened for ginger (Green) in December 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Hamirpur (Nadaun) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.caption: Solan (Himachal Pradesh) and Hamirpur (Nadaun) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported ginger (Green) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 14 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Solan reported a median ₹2,800 per quintal. Hamirpur (Nadaun) reported a median ₹3,750 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,000/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,000 per quintal, and Hamirpur (Nadaun) was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 189 km by road
scenes.caption: 189 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹41/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹592 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹380 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Hamirpur (Nadaun) report, the rule selects 13 of 14 modeled shipping days. 13 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹727 per quintal (₹524 under stress).
